reading.body:
Melva Wallace leads Huston-Tillotson University, a historically Black institution in Austin, Texas, positioning a historically marginalized educational sector within AI ecosystem conversations.

Her role as President and CEO of a historically Black university places her at an intersection relevant to AI infrastructure questions. Austin is among the fastest-growing data center markets in the United States, driven by power availability and real estate costs. Educational institutions in such markets face competing pressures: capital demands from AI buildout versus institutional missions rooted in access and equity.

The data shows only her current position and does not indicate her specific stance on AI, compute investment, or campus infrastructure policy. It does not clarify whether Huston-Tillotson has positioned itself around AI research, data center hosting, or compute training, or how institutional leadership navigates these questions. Her categorization as an "Advocate and Public Voice" suggests influence on narrative rather than direct operational control over physical infrastructure.
